prospect.name: Qasim Khawaja
prospect.occupation: Nurse anesthetist at a hospital, working in the operating room including anaesthesia for knee replacements, shoulder and back surgery. Mostly seated but moves around. Wakes at 5:30am; long and sometimes stressful shifts, some running until 7 or 9pm. Six months into the role after three years of study.
prospect.family_status: Girlfriend, living a block away and staying with her parents, waiting to move in and expecting an engagement ring. No children; planning them. She trains with him and cooks for him. Muslim — observed Ramadan in February and March.
prospect.training_background: Trains three to four times a week on an upper/lower split with an extra rehab-focused leg day. Long history of on-and-off training interrupted by injury. Background in recreational basketball, now playing pickup roughly monthly. Did a six-month online coaching programme about six years ago during COVID that went well until a shoulder injury ended it. Has a gym in his building and a physical therapist across the street. Describes himself as having accumulated the knowledge but never sustained the consistency. Self-describes as 'skinny fat' with weight around the midsection, at his heaviest. Has never done kettlebell work.
prospect.medical: Chronic bilateral knee pain from cartilage wear secondary to flat feet, valgus knees and an acute hip angle, compounded by years of outdoor basketball on concrete. He is explicit that this is degenerative rather than traumatic — 'a lot of the injuries are kind of like cartilage wearing down. So that's not necessarily something you can easily physical therapy away.' AT THE TIME OF THE CALL HE IS WEARING A KNEE SLEEVE TO GET THROUGH THE WORKDAY BECAUSE THE KNEE IS SWELLING. Plantar fasciitis managed with orthotics. Restricted left hip internal rotation confirmed in 90-90 testing; previously saw a specialist at $250 per session out of pocket and stopped on cost. Currently in physical therapy twice a week with sessions already booked for the coming weeks. Self-describes as highly injury-prone and known to pull muscles from imbalances or dehydration. Was ill for the whole of May with a severe respiratory infection. Prior shoulder injury six years ago. Was considering peptides for joint recovery.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No instalment plan was offered. Two things outside the standard structure were improvised instead. First, a one-month entry tier with no price ever stated, credited against the full fee — 'I'll send you for the one month. After one month, when you decide you want to move forward, you just top up that amount with the rest, yeah, to 6K. So you won't pay more.' Second, a $100 fully refundable deposit to hold a spot — 'Put down $100 deposit, totally refundable. When you come back and you don't want to do it, fine, we'll charge you back.' The prospect paid the $100.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: No formal guarantee was stated. Two informal assurances were given instead: an injury pause — 'even if that would happen, that you would get injured and you couldn't perform some movements, or worst-case scenario, you couldn't work out at all. We'll just pause the training with him until you can get back' — with no terms, and an injury-rate claim: 'Over 1,000 clients that he worked with, probably, I don't know, maybe a dozen, over six years.'

What was collected was a $100 fully refundable deposit to hold a spot, expressly conditional on a subsequent conversation with his partner — 'All right, man. $100 deposit is in. And I'll get her on board.'
The close rule does not apply: he did not verbally agree to move forward. His last substantive position was 'I don't think I can make this commitment right now.'

outcome.next_step: Prospect to speak to his girlfriend, then message the rep on WhatsApp to schedule a joint call with her and the rep so she has the full context before the purchase decision. The verbally agreed Trevor onboarding slot of Tuesday 30 June, 7:15pm Eastern was left unresolved.

notable.note: The longest call in the batch at ninety-four minutes and the most instructive. On the scored process it is the strongest in the corpus — it is the only call where the consequence frame actually ran, including the line-in-the-sand question verbatim, and phases 3, 4 and 6 are all textbook. It then produced no sale and three separate improvisations outside the offer: a one-month entry tier with no price, a $100 refundable deposit that contradicts the deposit policy the sales manager stated two days earlier, and a verbal injury-pause assurance with no terms. Most seriously, the prospect withdrew on clinical grounds he is professionally qualified to assess — he is a nurse anesthetist who anaesthetises patients for knee replacements — citing cartilage wear, a knee currently swelling enough to need a sleeve at work, and twice-weekly physical therapy already booked. He was answered with 'Are you a prophet?' and then told that strength training means 'you won't get injured'. He also stated he had not understood this would be a call where he was asked to pay.

quality.notes: Severe throughout, with several multi-minute blocks containing both sides under a single label — the stretch from roughly 00:23:00 to 00:25:00 and the block from 01:59 onward in the pillar presentation are the worst. The prospect's closing refusal at 01:23:02 and the rep's 'you really believe that I'm going to give up on you that easily?' are merged into one prospect-labelled block. An internal contradiction in the rep's cancer statistic ('50 percent... You mean 15? No, no, 15') appears to be transcription corruption rather than speech. A '$1,000' figure appears in the prospect's spouse reasoning and cannot be reconciled with any stated price; recorded but not relied upon. Roles read from content throughout.
